methods.label: Subtract interior angles from straight angles
methods.explanation:
Assume the polygon is convex and take one exterior angle at each vertex consistently. Let \(n\) be its number of sides. Each interior angle and its exterior angle sum to \(180^\circ\), so the exterior-angle sum is
\[
n\times180^\circ-(n-2)\times180^\circ=360^\circ.
\]

The wording “any polygon” needs a convention for concave polygons. For example, the boundary of three unit squares arranged in an L is a hexagon with five \(90^\circ\) turns in one direction and one \(90^\circ\) turn in the opposite direction. Their unsigned total is \(6\times90^\circ=540^\circ\). Counting the reverse turn negatively instead gives \(5\times90^\circ-90^\circ=360^\circ\).

Thus, under the usual convex-polygon convention, the answer is \(360^\circ\), choice A. Without that restriction or a consistently directed-angle convention, the unrestricted statement is ambiguous.
